enzyme_name: Bile acid 7-O-sulfotransferase (mL-STL / SULT2A8), a cytosolic PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase
organism_context: Mouse liver Sult2a8 is the characterised 7alpha-hydroxy-bile-acid-preferring enzyme; human SULT2A1 is the nearest orthologue
rationale: Feng et al. characterised Sult2a8 (mL-STL) as the PPARalpha-regulated mouse hepatic cytosolic sulfotransferase that 7-O-sulfonates 7alpha-hydroxy bile acids, which is exactly the tauro-alpha-muricholate 7-sulfate chemistry here; cytosolic SULTs are single-domain enzymes with one sulfuryl-transfer activity (homodimerisation is not bifunctionality).
direction_note: Sulfuryl transfer from PAPS to the bile acid is the physiological direction; no sulfotransferase resynthesises PAPS from a bile-acid sulfate in vivo, so ModelSEED's reverse-only call is not supported by the enzymology.

enzyme_name: Dopamine (catecholamine) sulfotransferase SULT1A3
organism_context: Human; SULT1A3/1A4 is the human-specific catecholamine sulfotransferase, highly expressed in gut and platelets
rationale: SULT1A3 is the dedicated human catecholamine sulfotransferase that sulfonates dopamine on its catechol hydroxyls (3-O major, 4-O minor); it is a single ~34 kDa cytosolic sulfotransferase domain with one catalytic activity.
direction_note: PAPS-dependent conjugation runs forward in vivo; aryl sulfotransferases show reverse sulfuryl transfer only in vitro with artificial donors such as p-nitrophenyl sulfate, never by consuming PAP plus dopamine sulfate at physiological pools.

enzyme_name: Iodothyronine sulfotransferase (SULT1A1, with SULT1E1 and SULT1B1)
organism_context: Human liver/placenta; rat orthologues characterised in parallel
rationale: Kester et al. systematically assigned sulfonation of 3,3',5'-triiodothyronine (reverse T3) and other iodothyronines to human SULT1A1, SULT1A2, SULT1B1 and SULT1E1; each is a single-domain cytosolic sulfotransferase with one catalytic activity.
direction_note: Thyroid-hormone sulfation is a committed inactivation/clearance step driven by PAPS; the reverse (PAP + rT3 sulfate -> PAPS) is not a physiological reaction.

enzyme_name: Iodothyronine sulfotransferase (SULT1A1, with SULT1B1 and SULT1E1)
organism_context: Human; 3,3'-T2 is the preferred iodothyronine substrate of SULT1A1/1B1
rationale: 3,3'-diiodothyronine is the best iodothyronine substrate of the human phenol sulfotransferases SULT1A1 and SULT1B1 in the Kester/Visser surveys; all are single-domain cytosolic SULTs with one sulfuryl-transfer activity.
direction_note: Same as the other iodothyronine sulfotransferase entries: PAPS-driven conjugation is unidirectional in vivo.

enzyme_name: unidentified PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase acting on 17beta-estradiol 17-O-glucuronide
rationale: No literature could be found for a sulfotransferase that sulfonates the glucuronate moiety of an estrogen glucuronide (the ChEBI name places the sulfate on C3 of the glucuronate, not on the steroid A-ring), so the catalysing protein is genuinely unidentified; the only safe statement is that the chemistry is a PAPS-dependent sulfuryl transfer.
direction_note: Whatever the enzyme, PAPS -> PAP sulfuryl transfer is the direction all PAPS-dependent sulfotransferases run; ModelSEED's reverse call would require PAPS synthesis from a sulfated conjugate.

enzyme_name: unidentified PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase acting on estriol 16-O-glucuronide
rationale: As for rxn56571, no characterised enzyme could be matched to sulfonation of the glucuronate residue of estriol 16-glucuronide; the double-conjugate estriol 3-sulfate 16-glucuronide is a documented human metabolite but its sulfation step is attributed to no specific SULT in the literature retrieved.
direction_note: PAPS-dependent sulfuryl transfer is unidirectional in vivo regardless of which SULT isoform carries it.

enzyme_name: unidentified PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase acting on estriol 17-O-glucuronide
rationale: Third member of the same estrogen-glucuronide sulfation block as rxn56571/rxn56573; no catalysing protein could be identified from the literature, so 'unknown' is the honest call rather than assuming a cytosolic SULT isoform.
direction_note: PAPS-dependent sulfuryl transfer is unidirectional in vivo regardless of which SULT isoform carries it.

enzyme_name: unidentified aminoglycoside 6-O-nucleotidyltransferase (ANT(6)/AadE-type) using GTP
rationale: The chemistry (NTP + streptomycin -> PPi + 6-O-nucleotidylstreptomycin) is that of the ANT(6) aminoglycoside nucleotidyltransferase resistance family, but no paper describing a GTP-dependent streptomycin 6-O-guanylyltransferase could be found, so the specific protein is unidentified; the related AadA is a single-domain nucleotidyltransferase whose 'dual specificity' is substrate breadth (streptomycin 3''-OH and spectinomycin 9-OH), not two catalytic activities.
direction_note: Nucleotidyl transfer with PPi release is pulled forward by inorganic pyrophosphatase and produces a stable released metabolite; reverse-only flux (PPi + guanylylstreptomycin -> GTP) is not a described activity.

enzyme_name: Lactase-phlorizin hydrolase (LPH), phlorizin-hydrolase (glycosylceramidase) catalytic site
organism_context: Mammalian small-intestinal brush-border membrane; the mature enzyme is one polypeptide carrying both sites
rationale: Phlorizin hydrolysis to phloretin plus glucose is the defining activity of the phlorizin-hydrolase site of LPH; mechanism-based labelling showed the two activities sit on two separate catalytic glutamates (Glu1273 and Glu1749) of a single polypeptide, which is a genuine fused bifunctional enzyme rather than a complex.
direction_note: Both LPH sites are hydrolases, so its bifunctionality does not explain the conflict; glycoside hydrolysis at cellular water activity is effectively irreversible forward, and the eQuilibrator +14 kJ/mol that drives ModelSEED's reverse call is implausible for O-glucoside hydrolysis.

enzyme_name: Lactase-phlorizin hydrolase (LPH), lactase catalytic site (alternative: cytosolic beta-glucosidase GBA3)
organism_context: Mammalian small-intestinal brush border; the same substrate set (3-O-, 4'-O- and 7-O-glucosides plus phlorizin) is the published LPH profile
rationale: Day et al. showed dietary flavonol and flavone glucosides, including 3-O-glucosides, are hydrolysed by the lactase site of LPH, a single polypeptide that also carries the distinct phlorizin-hydrolase site; the monofunctional cytosolic beta-glucosidase GBA3 is an alternative catalyst, so the bifunctional call carries medium confidence.
direction_note: Glycosidases hydrolyse; the reverse condensation of free glucose onto an aglycone is not a physiological beta-glucosidase flux, so ModelSEED's reverse-only call is wrong on enzymology regardless of the eQuilibrator sign.

enzyme_name: Lactase-phlorizin hydrolase (LPH), lactase catalytic site (alternative: cytosolic beta-glucosidase GBA3)
organism_context: Mammalian small-intestinal brush border; 4'-O-glucosides (cf. quercetin 4'-glucoside) are a documented LPH substrate class
rationale: Luteolin 4'-O-glucoside falls in the flavonoid 4'-O-glucoside class shown to be hydrolysed by the lactase site of LPH, which is bifunctional by virtue of a second, distinct phlorizin-hydrolase site on the same chain; GBA3 is a monofunctional alternative catalyst.
direction_note: Hydrolysis is the only physiological direction for a beta-glucosidase.

enzyme_name: Lactase-phlorizin hydrolase (LPH), lactase catalytic site (alternative: cytosolic beta-glucosidase GBA3)
organism_context: Mammalian small-intestinal brush border; prunin is naringenin 7-O-glucoside, the same 7-O-glucoside class as genistein/daidzein 7-glucoside
rationale: Flavonoid and isoflavone 7-O-glucosides are hydrolysed by the lactase site of LPH, a single polypeptide bearing two distinct glycosidase active sites; GBA3 is the monofunctional alternative.
direction_note: Hydrolysis is the only physiological direction for a beta-glucosidase.

enzyme_name: Lactase-phlorizin hydrolase (LPH), lactase catalytic site (alternative: cytosolic beta-glucosidase GBA3)
organism_context: Mammalian small-intestinal brush border
rationale: Eriodictyol 7-O-glucoside is a flavanone 7-O-glucoside, the substrate class shown to be deglycosylated by the lactase site of the bifunctional LPH; GBA3 is the monofunctional alternative catalyst.
direction_note: Hydrolysis is the only physiological direction for a beta-glucosidase.

enzyme_name: Lactase-phlorizin hydrolase (LPH), lactase catalytic site (alternative: cytosolic beta-glucosidase GBA3)
organism_context: Mammalian small-intestinal brush border; cosmetin is apigenin 7-O-glucoside
rationale: Apigenin 7-O-glucoside belongs to the flavone 7-O-glucoside class hydrolysed by the lactase site of LPH, whose second, mechanistically distinct phlorizin-hydrolase site makes it a true fused bifunctional enzyme; GBA3 is the monofunctional alternative.
direction_note: Hydrolysis is the only physiological direction for a beta-glucosidase.

enzyme_name: Benzoate-CoA ligase (BadA / BclA / BoxL), adenylation half-reaction
organism_context: Anaerobic and aerobic aromatic-degrading bacteria (Rhodopseudomonas palustris BadA, Burkholderia xenovorans box-pathway paralogues)
rationale: Benzoyl-AMP is the enzyme-bound adenylate intermediate of benzoate-CoA ligase, an ANL-superfamily adenylate-forming enzyme; the domain-alternation that performs adenylation then thioesterification is one overall ligase activity (EC 6.2.1.25), not two distinct catalytic activities, so this is monofunctional.
direction_note: CoA, the acceptor that makes the overall ligation irreversible, is absent from this half-reaction; the isolated adenylation step is freely reversible (it is the basis of the standard ATP-PPi exchange assay), so neither a forward-only nor a reverse-only bound reflects the enzymology - net forward flux comes only from thioesterification plus pyrophosphatase.

enzyme_name: Flavin-containing monooxygenase 1 (FMO1); the historic 'NAD(P)-dependent hypotaurine dehydrogenase, EC 1.8.1.3' is a misassignment
organism_context: Mammalian (human and mouse FMO1); Fmo1-null mice accumulate hypotaurine and are taurine-deficient
rationale: Veeravalli et al. showed in vivo and in vitro that FMO1, a single-domain flavin monooxygenase, is the enzyme that oxygenates hypotaurine to taurine, and that the 1962 assignment of this step to an NAD-dependent hypotaurine dehydrogenase was incorrect.
direction_note: The equation is the discredited dehydrogenase formulation with O2 omitted and NADP+ standing in as oxidant; the real reaction consumes O2 and NAD(P)H, which makes hypotaurine -> taurine strictly one-way, and reduction of the taurine sulfonate back to a sulfinate is not a known biological reaction.

enzyme_name: Anthranilate-CoA ligase PqsA, adenylation half-reaction
organism_context: Pseudomonas aeruginosa, first committed step of alkylquinolone (PQS/HHQ) quorum-signal biosynthesis
rationale: Coleman et al. identified PqsA as an anthranilate-coenzyme A ligase and Witzgall et al. solved its N-terminal domain with the anthraniloyl-AMP intermediate bound, matching this reaction exactly; like other ANL-superfamily ligases it performs one overall ligation in two half-reactions, which is not bifunctionality.
direction_note: Anthraniloyl-AMP is an enzyme-bound intermediate and CoA, the acceptor that sets irreversibility, is missing from the entry; the adenylation half-reaction itself is reversible (ATP-PPi exchange), so the direction is set by the downstream thioesterification and pyrophosphatase, not by this step.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous (non-enzymatic) 1,4-Michael addition of methanol to the hydroxyclavatol-derived ortho-quinone methide
organism_context: Penicillium crustosum / P. expansum clavatol pathway; the o-quinone methide arises by spontaneous dehydration of hydroxyclavatol made by the Fe(II)/2-oxoglutarate oxygenase ClaD
rationale: Fan et al. showed the hydroxyclavatol-derived ortho-quinone methide forms by spontaneous dehydration and that its subsequent 1,4-Michael additions are explicitly nonenzymatic; Liao et al. demonstrated the same o-QM couples to a wide range of nucleophiles under mild aqueous conditions, so no protein catalyses this alcohol-trapping step.
direction_note: The o-quinone methide is a transient, highly electrophilic species, so trapping by solvent methanol runs only toward the ether; the reverse (retro-Michael regenerating free o-QM) has no net flux.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous (non-enzymatic) 1,4-Michael addition of ethanol to the hydroxyclavatol-derived ortho-quinone methide
organism_context: Penicillium crustosum / P. expansum clavatol pathway
rationale: Same chemistry as rxn56852 with ethanol as the nucleophile; the ortho-quinone methide addition steps in this pathway were shown to be nonenzymatic, so there is no catalysing enzyme to classify.
direction_note: Trapping of the transient electrophilic o-quinone methide by ethanol is one-way; ModelSEED's reverse-only call would require the stable ether to spontaneously eliminate ethanol.

enzyme_name: unknown - most likely an uncatalysed intramolecular cyclodehydration of 2-aminobenzoylacetaldehyde
rationale: No enzyme could be found for this step; the close structural analogue 2-aminobenzoylacetyl-CoA is documented to undergo spontaneous intramolecular cyclization to 2,4-dihydroxyquinoline in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and the same aniline-nitrogen attack on the aldehyde followed by dehydration and aromatisation accounts for quinolin-4-ol here.
direction_note: Cyclodehydration to an aromatic quinolinol is driven by aromatisation and is effectively irreversible; ModelSEED's reverse would be hydrolytic ring-opening of an aromatic 4-quinolinol, which does not occur.

enzyme_name: Sphingosine N-methyltransferase (SAM-dependent; activity demonstrated in mouse brain, gene not identified)
organism_context: Mouse brain cytosol/membranes (Igarashi & Hakomori); the protein has never been cloned
rationale: The only characterisation of this activity is the 1989 demonstration of a SAM-dependent sphingosine N-methyltransferase in mouse brain producing N-methyl- and N,N-dimethylsphingosine; because no protein or gene has been assigned, mono- vs bifunctional cannot be determined.
direction_note: The entry lumps two successive N-methylations, but both are run by the same activity, and SAM -> SAH methyl transfer is thermodynamically one-way, so the reverse-only call is untenable.

enzyme_name: Phosphatidylethanolamine N-methyltransferase (PEMT; yeast Opi3/Pem2, plant phospholipid N-methyltransferase)
organism_context: Mammalian liver PEMT performs all three methylations; in yeast Cho2/Pem1 does the first and Opi3/Pem2 the second and third
rationale: The conversion of a phosphatidyl-N-methylethanolamine to the N,N-dimethyl species is the second methylation of the PE -> PC methylation pathway, carried out by PEMT in mammals and Opi3 in yeast; performing three sequential methylations is one catalytic activity applied to successive substrates, not polyfunctionality.
direction_note: SAM -> SAH methyl transfer onto an amine is effectively irreversible; a reverse-only bound would mean SAH-dependent demethylation of the phospholipid headgroup, which no methyltransferase does.

enzyme_name: Phosphatidylethanolamine N-methyltransferase (PEMT; yeast Opi3/Pem2, plant phospholipid N-methyltransferase)
organism_context: Same enzyme family as rxn56984; the di-18:3 species points at a plant/yeast PLMT rather than mammalian PEMT
rationale: Second headgroup methylation of a di-linolenoyl phosphatidyl-N-methylethanolamine, catalysed by the phospholipid N-methyltransferase of the PE -> PC pathway; a single SAM-dependent N-methyltransferase activity, so monofunctional despite acting iteratively.
direction_note: SAM -> SAH methyl transfer is one-way; reverse-only flux is not an enzymatic possibility here.

enzyme_name: Phosphatidylethanolamine N-methyltransferase (PEMT)
organism_context: Mammalian liver; the 16:0/22:6 species is the classic DHA-enriched PC that hepatic PEMT generates
rationale: Second of the three sequential headgroup methylations performed by PEMT, a single polytopic ER/MAM membrane protein with one SAM-binding catalytic activity; the three successive methylations are the same chemistry on successive substrates, which is not bi- or polyfunctionality.
direction_note: SAM -> SAH methyl transfer is one-way, so ModelSEED's reverse-only call cannot be right.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme - the net campesterol -> sitosterol conversion needs sterol side-chain desaturation, SMT2 C-24 methylation of the 24-methylene intermediate, and a final reductase step
organism_context: Plants (Arabidopsis SMT2/SMT3 control the campesterol:sitosterol ratio)
rationale: Plant sterol C-24 methyltransferase 2 methylates 24-methylenelophenol, not campesterol: a saturated 24-methyl sterol has no 24(28) double bond to accept a second methyl, so no characterised enzyme performs this entry as written, and the carbon bookkeeping only balances because an oxidation and a reduction cancel.
direction_note: Campesterol and sitosterol are products of two branches off 24-methylenelophenol rather than substrate and product of one step, so neither direction is a real in-vivo flux; if the entry is used at all, the SAM -> SAH methyl transfer forbids the reverse.
